narrative.overview: Each person's day is an index card, and checking in presses a rubber date stamp into a round slot. Cool card stock, hairline blue rules, blue-black ink, and two stamp inks, with neutral ink controls: violet for me, teal for my partner. Hierarchy by scale contrast, no boxes. Nothing is red; unchecked means not recorded.
keyCharacteristics: Index-card ground, hairline blue rules, blue-black ink.
Violet and teal are stamp inks, not UI accents; controls are neutral ink.
Rows are type plus a 48dp stamp slot on the right; no row borders or fills.
One big number per card, in the owner's ink.

rules.name: The Reserved Ink Rule
rules.body: Violet and teal appear only on stamps, punches, a person's own count and the owner's card spinner. Controls (FAB, buttons, chips, switches, tabs) use action, tonal and ink.

rules.name: The No Red Rule
rules.body: No red, no warning hue, anywhere. Overdue and unrecorded are stated in plain muted text.

rules.name: The Three Values Rule
rules.body: A screen is ground, ink and stamp. A fourth color needs a reason the build already shows.

rules.name: The Big Count Rule
rules.body: One display-size number per card; everything else stays at body size or below.

rules.name: The Tonal Only Rule
rules.body: Separate surfaces by ground-versus-card value, not by shadows or card borders around rows.

dos: Do express done state as a stamp in the owning person's ink, with a screen-reader label on every check.
Do separate rows with a hairline rule in rule, and give control borders faint so they meet 3:1.
Do show errors as ink text with an icon and an alert role.
Do keep the partner's card read-only and in teal.
Do honor reduce-motion for the stamp landing.
donts: Don't use red or any alarm hue for overdue, missed or unrecorded.
Don't add progress rings, streak flames, confetti or rainbow habit cards.
Don't put borders or fills around rows.
Don't use violet or teal for controls, tabs, buttons, chips or the FAB.
